Items.Authors: Jordan D. Wheeler, Jason Austermann, Anna K. Vaskuri, Michael Vissers, Johannes Hubmayr, James Beall, Jeffrey van Lanen, Johnathon Gard, Douglas Bennett, Joel Ullom
Items.Title: Low Tc KIDs for the far infrared
Items.Abstract: Low Tc detector materials for Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) can enhance sensitivity by reducing the superconducting gap energy and achieving longer quasiparticle lifetimes. In addition, higher normal-state resistivity can enable free-space impedance matching with less detector volume, further increasing detector sensitivity. We explore titanium-based materials, specifically low Tc TiN/Ti multilayer films and Al/Ti multilayer films, to lower Tc and increase resistivity. The potential of these films is evaluated with measurements of optical efficiency and noise-equivalent power (NEP) for far-infrared detector prototypes at 350 μm. The designs aim to enable high-filling-factor pixels without focal plane focusing optics for future far-infrared space applications.

Items.Authors: Brandon Mechtley, Matthieu Bec, Juan Carlos Guerra, Albert Conrad
Items.Title: Low-Latency Real-time Web Interfaces at the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory
Items.Abstract: This paper describes the motivation for and implementation of a distributed real-time telemetry pipeline for web interfaces at the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, including displays for the SOUL adaptive optics, telescope metrology, telescope status, and environmental subsystems. Increased demand for remote operation and more teams operating simultaneously has resulted in higher latency for remote X11 and X2Go sessions, motivating the development of a distributed web-based framework for telemetry dashboards and control interfaces. We have built this framework into our Data Mining System (DMS) using a ZeroMQ-websocket gateway, modular frontend interfaces using the LitElement web component framework, Redis for a key-value store and publish/subscribe messaging, and real-time charts using chart.js. Finally, we also discuss a searchable log and telemetry interface being developed at LBTO.

Items.Authors: Songxin Dai, Hangxin Ji, Haoran Yu, Cheng Liao, Lili Wang, Wei Guo, Mingming Xu
Items.Title: Low-resolution Fast Transient spectrograph for 3.8m telescope
Items.Abstract: The Low-resolution Fast Transient Spectrograph is a low-dispersion spectrograph jointly developed by the University of Science and Technology of China(USTC) and the Nanjing Institute of Astronomical Optics & Technology(NIAOT), for the 3.8-meter telescope at the Timau observation station in Indonesia. Its primary scientific objective is to conduct rapid and efficient spectroscopic follow-up observations of transient sources discovered in time-domain surveys. LOFTS covers a broad wavelength range from 370 nm to 1000 nm. When using a 1.3″ slit, the spectral resolution reaches R ≥ 750 at 495 nm and R ≥ 1000 at 750 nm; The peak optical efficiency of the spectrograph is no less than 35%, excluding losses from the slit and detector. This paper presents the detailed optical design of LOFTS and describes its mechanical structure and control system architecture.

Items.Authors: Hari B. Subedi, Scott D. Will, Alan Gostin
Items.Title: Lyot-based low-order wavefront sensor (LLOWFS) for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) coronagraph contrast stability required to differentiate planets from residual speckles in the dark hole and to detect planets with proper signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) drives very tight tolerances for wavefront variation. The wavefront needs to be stable within 10 pm over 10 minutes and the tip-tilt control needs to be at the sub-milliarcsecond level. Here we describe a Lyot-based low-order wavefront sensor (LLOWFS) for the Exploratory Analytic Case 1 (EAC1) design for the HWO using the scalar vortex coronagraph (SVC) to estimate dynamic low-order wavefront aberrations. The LLOWFS uses rejected starlight from the Lyot stop and slightly defocused images to infer thermally induced low-order aberrations. In this paper, we review the theory of LLOWFS operation, describe the LLOWFS algorithm, and summarize various numerical sensitivity studies on sensor performance.

Items.Authors: Nuno Morujão, Carlos Correia, Felipe Guzmán, Guillaume Bourdarot, Jean-Baptiste Le Bouquin, Denis Defrère, Frank Eisenhauer, Sebastian F. Hönig, Laura Kreidberg, Arseniy Kuznetsov, Romain Laugier, Thibaut Paumard, Esteban Vera Rojas, Paulo Garcia
Items.Title: Machine learning enforced fringe tracking control at the VLTI
Items.Abstract: Mitigating Optical Path Difference (OPD) jitter is critical for the VLTI's GRAVITY+ instrument. Current Kalman filtering yields residuals of 100–150 nm, limiting performance. We propose a Machine Learning (ML) approach to bridge the gap to the fundamental limit.    Using real on-sky telemetry and a calibrated simulator, we trained an LSTM neural network to control the fringe tracking loop. Comparing this with classical methods, we demonstrate that ML performs better in handling non-linear telescope vibrations.    This work lays the foundation for neural Real-Time Control. By targeting the ~30 nm atmospheric residual limit, this approach could allow a 14-fold increase in integration time. Consequently, this software-driven evolution unlocks a sensitivity gain of nearly three magnitudes, significantly expanding the scientific reach of the VLTI.

Items.Authors: Nico Soto, Povilas Palunas
Items.Title: MACO: updating active optics control for the Magellan telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present MACO (Magellan ACtive Optics), an effort to update the wavefront control software for the 6.5m Magellan telescopes. MACO implements modal wavefront control using an orthogonal basis in slope space spanning both primary and secondary mirror degrees of freedom, ensuring well-separated, non-degenerate control modes ordered by required force. The system provides real-time visualization for operation and offline analysis for troubleshooting, supporting both legacy and upgraded guide cameras. Engineering and commissioning results show geometrical residuals of 0.05" RMS with seeing-limited image quality, and actuator forces that settle within half the available range as observations progress.

Items.Authors: Ilse M. van Bemmel, John Romein, Vishnambar N. Pandey, Bram Veenboer, Steven van der Vlugt
Items.Title: Managing challenging procurement processes: the story of the high performance compute cluster for the Radioblocks project
Items.Abstract: The procurement of a new high performance compute cluster highlighted several challenges in the process. Grant providers and national depreciation rules are prohibitive of the necessary flexibility, making it difficult to work with the latest hardware and make choices for best efficiency and performance. I will discuss the issues in detail and propose solutions based on experience from the Radioblocks project.

Items.Authors: Jacob Pember, Ioannis Argyriou Tsikrikonis, Gerardo Ávila, Alexis Brandeker, Lars A. Buchhave, Heather Cegla, David W. Coutts, Wim De Meester, Joris De Ridder, Denis Defrère, Alistair Glasse, Manuel Güdel, Mariam Haidar, Kaustubh Hakim, Samuel P. Halverson, Joel Harman, Nicholas Jannsen, Markus Janson, Ailidh Kinney, Suzanne Kovacs, Romain Laugier, Christopher Miller, Kwinten Missiaen, Benjamin Montet, Johan Morren, Enric Pallé, Jesus Pérez Padilla, Wim Pessemier, Don Pollacco, Benjamin Pope, Saskia Prins, Andreas Quirrenbach, Gert Raskin, Maddalena Reggiani, Ignasi Ribas, Hugues Sana, Christian Schwab, Dries Seynaeve, Robyn Sharman, Julien Storm, Julian Stürmer, Giovanna Tinetti, Andrew Tkachenko, Hans Van Winckel, Bart Vandenbussche, Pieter Vuylsteke, Chris Waring, Rob Wittenmyer, Duncan Wright, Yanjun Zhou
Items.Title: MARVEL: approaching instrument assembly and commissioning
Items.Abstract: MARVEL is an upcoming dedicated radial velocity facility that will soon be commissioned at the Mercator Observatory at La Palma, Spain. MARVEL comprises four 0.8m telescopes, each feeding starlight via optical fibres into a single high-resolution spectrograph tuned for precision radial velocity measurements. The four telescopes and their domes have been successfully installed at the observatory site, and are regularly being used for initial photometric observations. In this proceeding we provide a general status update of the facility, and report on the procurement, assembly, and laboratory testing of the spectrometer optics and mechanics. We also highlight a few of the lessons learned thus far during MARVEL’s development ahead of final commissioning and anticipated first light in 2026.

Items.Authors: Jacob Pember, Gert Raskin, Christian Schwab, Johan Morren, Wim Pessemier, Jesus Pérez Padilla, Pieter Vuylsteke, Julien Storm, Bart Vandenbussche
Items.Title: MARVEL: design and implementation of the telescope front-end modules
Items.Abstract: MARVEL is an upcoming dedicated radial velocity facility that will soon be commissioned at the Mercator Observatory at La Palma, Spain. The MARVEL facility comprises four 0.8m telescopes, each feeding via optical fibres a single high-resolution spectrograph specialised for precision radial velocity measurements. Mounted on each MARVEL telescope is a front-end module providing several critical functions, including atmospheric dispersion correction, fast guiding capability, and efficient coupling of starlight—as well as calibration light—into the optical fibres. In this proceeding we present the design and development of these front-end modules and outline our plan for their integration at the observatory.

Items.Authors: Mariam Haidar, Gert Raskin, Christian Schwab, Julian Stuermer, Jacob Pember, Joris De Ridder, David Coutts, Tobias Feger, Daniel Krolikowski, Stanimir O. Letchev, Bart Vandenbussche, Hans Van Winckel
Items.Title: MARVEL: updates to the calibration system and strategy
Items.Abstract: Stable and precise wavelength calibration is absolutely critical in measuring the radial velocity (RV) signatures imparted on stellar hosts by extrasolar planetary companions. The MARVEL (Mercator Array for Radial VELocities) facility will host a cross-dispersed, high-resolution echelle spectrograph, fiber-fed by four 0.8m telescopes, with the resulting spectra recorded on a single detector alongside that of a simultaneous calibration source. This dedicated surveying facility will provide essential ground-based RV follow-up on transit measurements by previous and upcoming space missions. MARVEL aims for an RV measurement precision of 1 m/s, requiring a suite of state-of-the-art calibration tools and techniques capable of developing a wavelength solution stable to the sub-m/s level over long timescales. In this work, we provide an overview of the inner workings of the MARVEL calibration unit and outline updates made to our calibration strategy in anticipation of first light in 2026.

Items.Authors: Dionne M. Haynes, Andrew Kruse, Antony Galla, Gregory Jolley, Trevor Mendel, Israel Vaughn, David Brodrick, Jesse Cranney, François Rigaut, Gaston Gausachs, Tristan Monnier, Warrick Schofield, Annino Vaccarella, Hana Benhizia, Brian Taylor, Julien Bernard, Jennifer Burgess, Roger Haynes, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Bernardo Salasnich, Mirko Colapietro, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Davide Greggio, Elia Costa, Matteo Aliverti, Luca Marafatto, Valentina Viotto, Maria Bergomi, Enrico Pinna, Giovanni Cresci, Guido Agapito, Salvatore Savarese, Daniela Fantinel, Rosanna Sordo, Simonetta Chinellato, Anthony Horton, Ross Zhelem, Simon Ellis, Richard McDermid, Nuria Lorente, Nuwanthika Fernando, Brent Miszalski, Lew Waller, Timothy Chin, Max Hewlett, Scott Smedley, Pierre Haguenauer, Stefan Ströbele, Ulf Seemann
Items.Title: MAVIS: calibration unit final design
Items.Abstract: The MAVIS Calibration Unit (CU) is a dedicated subsystem of the MCAO-Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph (MAVIS) instrument for the ESO Very Large Telescope (VLT). Its primary role is to deliver precise calibration for the Imager, Spectrograph, and Adaptive Optics Module, ensuring optimal scientific performance. The CU design incorporates multiple modules—Main Calibration Module (MCM), Light Source Module (LSM), Astrometric Calibration Module (ACM), and Calibration Control Module (CCM)—to support a wide range of calibration functions, including optical distortion correction, non-common-path aberration calibration, spectral calibration, flat-fielding, wavefront sensor alignment, and instrument alignment. The design integrates advanced opto-mechanical assemblies, precision motion stages, and robust control systems to ensure high accuracy and reliability under operational conditions at the VLT. This paper presents the CU final design, detailing the architecture, interfaces, optical a

Items.Authors: Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Valentina Viotto, Francois Rigaut, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Jesse Cranney, Guido Agapito, Maria Bergomi, Enrico Pinna, Andrea Baruffolo, Bernardo Salasnich, Daniela Fantinel, Mirko Colapietro, Elia Costa, Pierre Haguenauer, David Brodrick, Richard McDermid, Dionne Haynes, Antony Galla, Andrew Kruse
Items.Title: MAVIS: calibration, estimation, and removal of the non-common path aberrations
Items.Abstract: MAVIS is a multi-conjugate adaptive optics–assisted imager and IFU spectrograph for ESO’s VLT (UT4), operating in the visible. Its adaptive optics module (AOM) provides a uniform 30″ field of view using eight laser guide stars, up to three natural guide stars, and three deformable mirrors. As MAVIS is designed for high-precision astrometry, stringent requirements are imposed on optical quality and residual wavefront error (WFE). Under standard observing conditions, the AOM must deliver an average Strehl ratio ≥8% (goal 12%) for three NGSs with mJ≈8, corresponding to a science-channel WFE of 139 nm (goal 127 nm). This requires calibration and compensation of non-common-path aberrations (NCPAs). MAVIS adopts tomographic phase diversity (TPD), a focal-plane method that estimates aberrations directly from science images and optimises correction using all deformable mirrors. We present the NCPA strategy from laboratory integration to on-sky implementation.

Items.Authors: Hrushikesha Athreya, Mazhar Ali, James Cornelison, Mischa Mikhailov, Roald van der Kolk, Jessica Zebrowski
Items.Title: Measurements of low-loss dielectrics for line intensity mapping detectors
Items.Abstract: Low-loss on-chip spectrometers offer a promising technology to achieve higher sensitivities for line-intensity mapping (LIM) experiments. Improving the dielectric loss in the thin-film dielectric layer separating the superconducting microstrip from the ground plane could increase the overall sensitivity of these detectors. To address this, we present microwave (4.6-6.7 GHz) cryogenic loss measurements of nanofabricated microstrip test devices for materials such as silicon nitride (SiNx) and silicon carbide (SiC). These were fabricated using Inductively Coupled Plasma Chemical Vapor Deposition (ICPCVD) which allows for low-temperature deposition. Our results demonstrate some of the lowest dielectric losses for SiC deposited by ICPCVD and we discuss the correlation between silicon fraction and low-temperature loss. These measurements will inform the material selection and design of next-generation on-chip spectrometers for LIM instruments.

Items.Authors: Gilles Orban de Xivry, Olivier Absil, Thomas Bertram, Roy van Boekel, André Boné, Gaël Chauvin, Valentin Christiaens, Dennis Dolkens, Iain Hammond, Gilles Otten, Prashant Pathak, Nuno Pereira
Items.Title: METIS high-contrast imaging simulations: from instrument modeling to science readiness
Items.Abstract: The High-contrast End-to-End Performance Simulator (HEEPS) has been updated to support the Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) high-contrast imaging science preparation. Key improvements include final pupil/Lyot stop modeling, as-built NCPA/Talbot effect simulations, and advanced NCPA control strategies using the ALF algorithm. We present comprehensive HCI performance simulations across L-, M-, and N-bands and multiple observing modes, producing updated contrast curves and PSF images. These results demonstrate HEEPS' critical role in bridging METIS instrumentation and scientific readiness for the ELT era.

Items.Authors: Johannes Hubmayr, Jason E. Austermann, Kyuyoung Bae, James E. Beall, Jake E. Connors, Shannon M. Duff, Gregory Jaehnig, Matthew Koc, Michael Link, Tammy Lucas, Christopher Rooney, Corwin Shiu, Joel N. Ullom, Michael R. Vissers
Items.Title: Millimeter-wave component design of OMT-coupled TES detectors
Items.Abstract: Planar Ortho-Mode Transducer coupled transition edge sensor (TES) bolometer arrays fabricated at NIST have been used in instruments such as Advanced ACTPol, SPIDER, and Simons Observatory for measurements of Cosmic Microwave Background polarization. Within each spatial pixel, these devices measure orthogonal polarizations in multiple frequency bands. We present the millimeter-wave design of the on-chip components, which include a coplanar waveguide to microstrip transition, diplexer, stepped impedance low pass filter, microstrip cross-over, 180 degree hybrid, and millimeter-wave power termination located on the TES bolometer island. Focusing on a 90/150 GHz dichroic design, the simulated coupling efficiency of the integrated pixel exceeds 80% in both bands and the cross-polarization is < 0.5%.

Items.Authors: Paul Tagnon, Damien Prêle, Manuel Gonzalez, Michel Piat, Alessandro Monfardini, Martino Calvo, Emile Prêle, Faouzi Boussaha
Items.Title: Millimetric back-shorted coplanar wave guide optimization for quarter wavelength spectrometers
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present the design of a fully coplanar waveguide back shorted dual quarter wavelength spectrometer.  The dual quarterwave length is equivalent to a long open transmission line where we added a shunt inductance to create a high frequency quarter wavelength on one side (filter) and a readout frequency quarter wavelength on the other side (MKID).  Adding a backshort to the feedline increases the transmitted power up to near 100% to the MKID.  We first present a simple circuit equivalent of the proposed spectrometer and the optimizations methods used.  Then the model was implemented on Sonnet where we considered the main fabrication constraints.

Items.Authors: Peter P. Pedersen, Lionel Garcia, David Degen, Didier Queloz
Items.Title: MIRA: Automating the observation lifecycle for educational access to robotic telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present the design of MIRA, a data management and educational platform that connects Swiss secondary school students and ETH Zurich undergraduates with operational robotic observatories. The system manages teacher-reviewed observation proposals and automates scheduling and data reduction. It also provides structured access to archived observations.  Users submit observation proposals, specifying targets and scientific objectives. Approved proposals are then scheduled and following execution, raw FITS frames undergo automated processing. Users can retrieve observations via a web interface and follow Python-based tutorials for data reduction and analysis.  This design gives students an authentic experience of professional astronomical workflows, including proposal development, observational scheduling, data reduction and analysis. We describe the system architecture, its integration with observatory control software, the proposal workflow and the development plan across three phases.

Items.Authors: Michael Esselborn, Henri Bonnet, Carlos Diaz Cano, Byron Engler, Aglaé Kellerer, Johannes Kolmeder, Oliver Pfuhl, Adam Rubin, Christophe Vérinaud, Julien Woillez
Items.Title: Mitigating pupil distortion for robust ELT phasing with SHAPS
Items.Abstract: The Shack-Hartmann Phasing Sensor (SHAPS) is the baseline instrument for cophasing the segmented 39-m primary mirror of the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). Located in the Phasing and Diagnostics Station (PDS), SHAPS employs a modified Shack-Hartmann design to re-image the full 798-segment primary onto a high-precision lenslet array. Meeting the requirement of < 12 mm mapping accuracy in the M1 space is critical for achieving the phase tolerances needed for diffraction-limited performance. Given the tight registration and distortion tolerances, distortion effects pose a significant risk to the SHAPS phasing concept.  We present a risk-mitigation strategy that combines in-field measurement of the as-built pupil distortion during the WFC commissioning phase with the fabrication of a new lenslet array in which the average distortion is deliberately imprinted. The strategy has been successfully validated on the Miniscule ELT (MELT) test bench, demonstrating its feasibility for ELT phasing.

Items.Authors: Jed Diller
Items.Title: Modeling and expected performance of the GNAO LGSF jitter loop
Items.Abstract: Gemini North Adaptive Optics (GNAO) is a next-generation system that enables near-diffraction-limited observations using laser guide stars and adaptive optics. This work focuses on the Fast Pointing Loop (jitter loop) in the Laser Guide Star Facility, which stabilizes the four side-launched laser guide stars on the wavefront sensors to within 0.01 arcseconds as the asterism rotates on the sodium layer. The loop’s performance depends on computational latency and the dynamics of fine steering mirrors and hexapods. A discrete controls model was developed to evaluate bandwidth, sensitivity to latencies, seeing conditions, and controller tuning. The model is validated with historical data and component testing and will support commissioning, tuning, and diagnosing unexpected system behavior.

Items.Authors: Jeff W. Richey, Robert L. Johnson, Lauren Schatz, Simon Rochester
Items.Title: Modeling of 75-W sodium beacon
Items.Abstract: The Starfire Optical Range has completed on-sky testing with a new 75-W sodium laser guide star (LGS) system from Toptica Photonics which includes various laser advancements including single-side band repumping, frequency broadening, and a frequency chirping capability. Given the large parameter space available with this advanced laser system, accurate modelling of the return flux is necessary to inform system tuning and optimization. We will present modeling results from an updated version of the well-known LGS Bloch code and compare them to on-sky results and investigate options for refining the model to yield better agreement with test results. Finally, we will use the model to inform future LGS development particularly for the case of pre-compensation where the higher peak irradiance should maximize the benefit of frequency chirping.

Items.Authors: Guillermo Pascual-Cisneros, Stefano Della Torre, Anaïs Besnard, Francisco J. Casas, Paolo Dal Bo, Gregory Jaehnig, Bruno Maffei, Tomotake Matsumura, Francesco Piacentini, Valentin Sauvage, Andrea Tartari, Mario Zannoni, Samantha Stever, Massimo Gervasi, Giovanni Signorelli
Items.Title: Modeling of the thermal systematics produced by cosmic rays hits in a sub-K bolometric array placed on L2
Items.Abstract: The next generation of cosmic microwave background (CMB) instruments aim to reach unprecedented sensitivities, making the characterization and mitigation of instrumental systematic effects increasingly critical. One key effect for space-based CMB missions is the impact of Cosmic Rays (CRs).  In this context, we present a simulation pipeline to simulate time ordered energy deposition data produced by hits of different CR particles on a given focal plane configuration. This data is then used to model thermal fluctuations on the wafer with a custom two-dimensional heat equation solver optimized for this problem, that has been validated against COMSOL Multiphysics simulations.   This pipeline is applied to LiteBIRD satellite configuration finding that thermal fluctuations produced by CR hits can be understood as an additional white-noise contribution comparable to current instrumental requirements, underscoring the need for CR-mitigation techniques.

Items.Authors: Julien Drevon, Claudia Paladini, Peter L. Scicluna, Isabelle Percheron, Akke Corporaal
Items.Title: Modeling the VLTI/PIONIER transfer function using machine learning
Items.Abstract: We developed a machine learning framework to model the interferometric Transfer Function (TF) of the VLTI/PIONIER instrument using environmental and instrumental parameters such as seeing, coherence time (τ₀), pressure, temperature, baseline, and wavelength. The goal was to predict and monitor TF variations in real time to improve calibration accuracy. After testing several models, we adopted eXtreme Gradient Boosting, which worked efficiently on both small and large datasets while providing stable and interpretable results. Using over 45,000 visibility measurements collected between 2022 and 2024, the model achieved an R² of about 0.98 on both training and test sets, showing strong predictive performance and generalization. Feature analysis with Variation Inflation Factor and SHapley Additive exPlanations showed that baseline, wavelength, and pressure were the most influential parameters. These findings show that machine learning can provide a reliable solution for TF predictions.

Items.Authors: Icíar Montilla Garcia, Luzma Montoya, Marcos Reyes García-Talavera, Peter Wizinowich, Mitchell Troy, Javier Castro, Héctor de Paz, Sergio Fernández, Manuel Huertas, Gianluca Lombardi, Daniel Gómez, Ismael Álvarez, Josep Miret
Items.Title: Modelling atmospheric dispersion effects on fine phasing of large segmented mirrors
Items.Abstract: The Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC), with its segmented primary mirror, needs precise fine phasing for optimal performance. Atmospheric dispersion, which separates light into wavelengths due to atmospheric refraction, can disrupt segment alignment, especially in optical bands when using broadband algorithms. This study investigates the impact of dispersion on cophasing and proposes an atmospheric dispersion model to improve the process. The model estimates distortions caused by dispersion during cophasing, allowing separate measurement of segment piston and dispersion effects, reducing errors. Preliminary results show that correcting for atmospheric dispersion enhances image quality and segment alignment. The model offers a valuable tool for improving segmented mirror telescopes and can be applied to other large-scale observatories.

Items.Authors: Anthony Meilland, Philippe Priolet, Jean-Charles Augereau, Steve Ertel, Thomas Stuber, Jeremy B. Scott, Romain Laugier, Denis Defère
Items.Title: Modelling NOTT nulling-interferometric data using oimodeler and GRaTer
Items.Abstract: We present preparatory work for modeling future data from the VLTI/NOTT instrument, to be installed at Paranal next year as part of the ASGARD suite. Unlike conventional interferometers, NOTT will operate in nulling mode, cancelling stellar light to achieve high contrast and reveal faint nearby material such as exoplanets or circumstellar dust. Because nulling interferometry produces multiple flux measurements depending on the nulling pattern rather than standard observables, its data cannot be stored in OIFITS2 and efforts are underway to define a dedicated NIFITS format. oimodeler, a modular Python package for optical-interferometry modeling fully compatible with OIFITS, has been extended to simulate NIFITS data for NOTT. Our simulations focuses on two main science cases: detecting and characterizing faint binaries and exoplanets, and modeling exozodiacal dust. For the latter, we integrated pyGRaTer an updated python version of the GRaTer radiative-transfer code into oimodeler.

Items.Authors: Manal Chebbo, Laurent Jocou, Patrick Rabou, David Mouillet, Louis Barbier, Lorenzo Busoni, Simonetta Chinellato, Paolo Ciliegi, Jean-Jacques Correia, Andrea Di Rocco, Jacopo Farinato, Italo Foppiani, Sylvain Guieu, Yves Magnard, Demetrio Magrin, Thibaut Moulin, Fabrice Pancher, Marco Riva, Sylvain Rochat, Sébastien Soler, Ludovico Teodori
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: laser guide stars module
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  We present a completed and consistent design for the MORFEO LGSWFS Module, which consists mainly of 6 Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors mounted on a high-precise rotating and translating platform designed to track the ELT elevation axis. This design satisfies demanding specifications required to achieve high-accuracy wavefront sensing on the ELT.   A key element of each sensor is its micro-lens array (MLA), based on an innovative symmetric double-sided design that ensures telecentricity of the exit beam.   This paper presents the architecture and expected performance of the MORFEO LGSWFS Module, focusing on the rotator, focusing stage, and MLA technologies that enable high-accuracy wavefront sensing on the ELT.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: Mechanical alignment system for MORFEO optomechanics
Items.Abstract: The MORFEO’s optomechanics are going toward the FDR the interfaces are defined and the alignment system is tested in our lab to prove the designed alignment range and the repeatability of the system. The methodology followed for the characterization of the mechanics is made of three different parts. The first one is the characterization of the kinematics connection, the second on the measure of the single alignment system based on wedge solution. The third step is the metrology of the whole system. In this proceeding it will e reported the final results of the measurement campaign pointing out the different solution used and final design.

Items.Authors: Daphne Diretto, Andrea Baruffolo, Mirko Colapietro, Elia Costa, Benedetta Di Francesco, Daniela Fantinel, Fulvio Laudisio, Fabrice Pancher, Bernardo Salasnich
Items.Title: MORFEO@ELT: latest update in the instrument control system software design
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. It provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. Thanks to the progress toward the Final Design Review, we present the latest updates to the design of the MORFEO Instrument Control System Software (ICSS). We examine the design approaches and the current work dedicated to guarantee high robustness, modularity, and seamless integration with the ELT software framework. Particular focus will be given to its integration with the MICADO ICSS. We then introduce SAPO (Software for AIT Phase Operation), a dedicated instrument with its control software designed to support the MORFEO assembly, integration and testing phase.

Items.Authors: Jose-Miguel Ibáñez Mengual, Sergio Rodríguez, Fernándo Álvarez, Rocío Calvo, Isabel Bustamante, Héctor Magán, Jorge Iglesias
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: Status of the low-level control system for the NIR-spectrograph cryogenic mechanisms.
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object fibre spectrograph for ESO's 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT),currently progressing in its design phase. Its near-infrared spectrograph, incorporates four cryogenic mechanisms: two for the entrance focal plane exchanger and two for the H-band low-/high-resolution grating exchanger. These mechanisms are distributed across two cryogenic benches, each hosting one unit of each type. This paper presents an overview of the current design and prototyping of the Low-Level Electronic Instrument Control System (LL-EICS), developed by IAA-CSIC, to operate these mechanisms. The LL-EICS is implemented on the ESO ELT Instrument Framework, which supplies the communication layer, mechanism-control services, and interfaces to telescope and observation software. We describe the system architecture—built on Beckhoff PC-based control technology, EtherCAT real-time networks, and modular electronics and show how this design enables deterministic motion and reliable operation.

Items.Authors: Marc R. Baril, Gregory A. Green, William Mahoney, Conrad Holmberg, Cameron Wipper
Items.Title: Nānā ao: an all-sky, weather-ready LWIR & visible imager for Maunakea
Items.Abstract: A full view of the night sky is invaluable for observers as they seek to queue their observations to avoid cloudy, non-photometric conditions. Imaging in the LWIR band, 8 – 14 µm, allows for the detection of thin cloud cover, whereas visible band imaging can indicate the arrival of thick cloud banks. Maunakea’s all-sky LWIR/VIS imager was recently redesigned to provide a more weather-robust enclosure and support newer sensors. This instrument, Nānā ao, replaces the ASIVA instrument that had been in service since 2010. In addition to the mechanical improvements made, this project represents an early instance of development within the framework of Gitlab’s continuous-integration/development (CI/CD) environment at the Canada France Hawaii Telescope.

Items.Authors: Joshua Montgomery, Graeme Smecher, Michel Adamic, Matt Dobbs, Maclean Rouble, Ketan Sand, Sofiia Savchyn
Items.Title: New implementation of online triggering for KID pulse detection at µs-timescale
Items.Abstract: Applications that deploy Kinetic Inductance Detector (KID) arrays for pulse detection, such as for particle-physics and photon-counting, often require >1 MHz of readout bandwidth to recover pulse shapes and arrival times. Multiplexed arrays require enormous data throughput, so pulse triggers are typically implemented in firmware onboard the readout. These triggers are resource intensive and have limited functionality. We introduce a client-side triggering architecture that addresses these limitations using the 1/10/25/100 GbE networking throughput of the Radio Frequency System on a Chip (RFSoC)-based t0.CRS system. We demonstrate real-time pulse detection and capture with 2.44 MHz of complex bandwidth for up to 600 channels while maintaining visibility into the full-rate data. The online trigger includes dynamic thresholding, multi-sample coincidence logic, and matched filtering. We demonstrate first end-to-end measurements of triggered pulse events with a variety of KID devices.

Items.Authors: Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, Bojan Nikolic, Christopher L. Carilli, Laura Torino, Ubaldo Iriso
Items.Title: New techniques for high-resolution imaging and high-precision wavefront sensing via masked-aperture interferometry
Items.Abstract: We present novel techniques for high-precision wavefront sensing and high-resolution imaging using masked-aperture interferometry. Inspired by radio interferometry, these approaches can measure both the amplitude and phase of wavefront distortions while simultaneously reconstructing the source structure. We have demonstrated them on the ALBA synchrotron beamline. The first uses non-redundant aperture masks with a self-calibration algorithm to recover nanometer-scale pathlength errors and subarcsecond-scale source structure. The second employs closure invariants from these masks bypassing self-calibration while retaining comparable fidelity. The third extends self-calibration to redundant masks, enabling higher photon throughput without compromising reconstruction performance. These methods form a robust framework for high-resolution interferometry in photon-limited cases with applications from accelerator diagnostics to astronomical facilities like the James Webb Space Telescope.

Items.Authors: Juan M. Altamirano, James Luis, David Buscher, Chris Haniff, Bodie Seneta
Items.Title: Next-generation metrology electronics and communication architecture for optical delay lines at MROI
Items.Abstract: This paper presents modernization of the MROI delay line metrology system addressing VME platform obsolescence while enhancing performance. The fiber-optic digital architecture replaces the 200-meter analog link, achieving sub-5 microsecond latency and 10-20 kHz sampling (2-4× improvement) while eliminating electromagnetic vulnerability from lightning strikes. Custom digital signal processing electronics replace obsolete VME hardware, improving low-light sensitivity critical for tracking very dim stars and faint astronomical objects. Working prototypes enable laboratory testing and spare delay line integration. Expected improvements include faster position correction during slewing operations, enhanced disturbance rejection via increased servo bandwidth, and improved optical path difference stability for fringe tracking. This offers a practical modernization pathway extending operational lifetime while significantly enhancing interferometric observation capabilities.

Items.Authors: Grecia Falcon, Imraan Bokhari, Eric Grigel
Items.Title: ngVLA 18m Antenna Preliminary Foundation Study
Items.Abstract: The ngVLA main antenna array is comprised of 244 antennas, with its core located at the VLA site in New Mexico and extending across multiple states, including sites in Mexico. While the core location is well established, the remaining antenna sites are still under evaluation. To assess the influence of soil variability on the 18-m antenna foundation, a study was conducted to identify an optimal preliminary foundation design that could be implemented across different site conditions with minimal modification. This paper presents an overview of the study and provides insight into how variations in soil properties affect the rotational stiffness of the foundation and, ultimately, the antenna pointing error. The findings from this work support the project’s planning efforts by guiding site selection, foundation design standardization, and overall construction cost optimization.

Items.Authors: Timothy M. C. Abbott, Jesse Ball, Heidi Schweiker, Eric J. Christensen, Ariel Lopez, John P. Blakeslee
Items.Title: Night-time operations under NOIRLab
Items.Abstract: As part of the introduction of matrix management, NOIRLab's night-time telescope operations and observing staff have been combined into the Telescope Operations group. These are the front line personnel at any observatory. They work under unusual pressures, and are uniquely key to the success of the astronomical exercise. We have integrated several long-established, distinct, and individually effective philosophies, plus Rubin's new approach, into an overarching structure which enables evolution into greater unity, mutual support, and responsiveness to NOIRLab's needs, without degrading each site's ability to operate their own facility with their customary maximum efficiency. In this paper, we discuss the roles of the night staff at NOIRLab's diverse observatories, how they meet the various demands at each facility, the challenges of managing these critical workers across multiple sites and professional cultures, and the lessons we have learned doing so over the past 5 years.

Items.Authors: Joseph G. Redford, Peter S. Barry, Chris Benson, Charles M. Bradford, Thomas Brien, Simon Doyle, Victor Gómez-Rivera, Steven Hailey-Dunsheath, Jesús Hernández-Aguilar, José Luis Hernández-Rebollar, David H. Hughes, Elijah Kane, Kirit Karkare, Alex M. Lapuente, Ryan McGeehan, Raúl Naranjo-Romero, Andreas Papageorgiou, Iván Rodríguez-Montoya, Sam Rowe, David Sánchez-Argüelles, Sofia Savorgnano, Annie Tan, Marcial Becerril-Tapia, Jair Vega-Méndez
Items.Title: Noise and sensitivity analysis of SuMaC on-sky and in lab
Items.Abstract: We present the on sky sensitivity of the SuperSpec-MUSCAT Collaboration (SuMAC). SuperSpec is a microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID) based on-chip spectrometer with an R ~ 200 covering 200 - 300 GHz band. In July of 2025, SuperSpec devices were installed into the MUSCAT instrument and observed on-sky at the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT) in July and August.  The spectral characterization and performance of the individual channels will be discussed, both in lab testing and the performance on-sky in the SuMAC setup, along with the extrapolated sensitivities of optimal conditions at the LMT.

Items.Authors: Marco Xompero, Armando Riccardi, Nicolò Azzaroli, Runa Antonio Briguglio Pellegrino, Giorgio M. Pariani, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Matteo Menessini
Items.Title: Novel approach to a stitched optical surface reconstruction
Items.Abstract: Large optics have become mandatory with the new generation of large telescope, in which not only the primary mirror is segmented. In this work we are introducing a new approach to estimate the optical surface of a mirror. With using partial surface measurement like in a standard stitching approach, we will populate our surface estimation using a continuously refined reconstructor optimum in a least-square way, converging to a stable solution granting surface continuity. We will estimate in the same time the cavity error and the alignment error for each single measurement of the partial optical surface..The base chosen for the estimation are the Zernike modes by Noll. Optical surfaces will be estimated together with caviry and alignment in a single minimization process.

Items.Authors: Glenn P. Brossus, Marianne Cox, Richard Demers, Barbara Fischer, Frank Groark, William Burgett
Items.Title: NSF sponsored risk reduction for the giant magellan telescope (GMT)
Items.Abstract: The NSF has supported risk reduction and prototyping efforts for the US Extremely Large Telescope program, that includes both the Giant Magellan Telescope and the Thirty Meter Telescope. The NSF Sponsored awards, and their impact on the Giant Magellan Telescope are presented herein. Three Awards received over the last 5 years have built and tested hardware that reduce risk, validate designs and verify performance of subsystems required for GMT active and adaptive optics control and performance. The NSF-Development subaward received from AURA built a primary mirror mounting cell and mirror support hardware, the long lead optics and main structural components for the first off-axis adaptive secondary mirror, and two wavefront sensing and control (WFSC) testbeds. Two subsequent awards utilized NSF built hardware to demonstrate active optics performance. Additional work included prototyping Real-Time Computing (RTC) platforms, and the Observatory Control System End-2-End Prototype.

Items.Authors: Julien Storm, Gert Raskin, Bart Vandenbussche, Christian Schwab, Jake Pember, Hugues Sana, Dirk Vandepitte, Leonardo Peri, Sibo Van Gool, Louis Storm, Pierre Royer, Maddalena Reggiani, Camille Pirat, Dominic Bowman
Items.Title: Onboard wavelength calibration of the CubeSpec high resolution spectrograph using a Fiber Fabry–Pérot Etalon
Items.Abstract: CubeSpec is a 12U CubeSat mission designed to demonstrate high resolution spectroscopy from a compact platform, with launch readiness targeted for early 2027. Its cross dispersed echelle spectrograph requires an onboard calibration system that is very compact, mechanically robust, and sufficiently stable and precise to meet the mission’s spectral performance requirements. A fiber-based Fabry–Pérot (FFP) etalon provides an attractive solution due to its very small footprint and stable line spacing, though it demands careful thermal stabilization. CubeSpec employs a fiber-coupled LED continuum source to both illuminate the FFP etalon for wavelength calibration and to supply broadband light for order identification and flat-fielding. The light is injected into the spectrograph via optics mounted on the telescope’s secondary mirror. We describe here the design of the FFP calibration unit and its expected performance.

Items.Authors: Eliad Peretz, Bert Pasquale, Guangjun Gao, Greg Aldering, Saul Prlmutter, Jerry Edelstein, Tim Miller
Items.Title: Optical and mechanical development of the ORKID-II multi-field integral field spectrograph using monolithic machined image slicers
Items.Abstract: ORKID-II is a next-generation integral field spectrograph designed for high-resolution, multi-field imaging and spectroscopy on large ground-based telescopes and future space missions. Building on the ORCAS/ORKID program, the instrument uses monolithic machined image slicers manufactured with sub-micron precision to enable fine, coarse, and very coarse spatial sampling within a compact optical platform. We present the optical and mechanical development of the tri-field IFU, including telecentric, anamorphic, and magnification-optimized designs; Canon-fabricated slicer geometries; system-level packaging; and integration with the telescope relay and spectrograph. ORKID-II demonstrates a scalable approach to wide-field, high-throughput spectroscopy and provides a technology path for future flagship observatories.

Items.Authors: Runa Briguglio, Marco Xompero, Giorgio Pariani, Nicolò Azzaroli, Luca Oggioni, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Riccardo Grignaffini, Armando Riccardi
Items.Title: Optical calibration of ELT-M4: segment phasing procedure tested on the prototype
Items.Abstract: A critical calibration in segmented optical system is the phasing, i.e. the accurate positioning of the segments, in both rotation and piston, in order to approximate a continuous surface. In deformable mirrors, the phasing is part of the flattening procedure and is obtained by the actuators; as a consequence, both high order shapes and rigid body motions shall be controlled accurately.  In this paper we describe the phasing procedure optimized for the ELT adaptive mirror M4 on its Optical Test Tower, and verified on the M4 Demonstration Prototype. The procedure includes the high orders flattening, based on the actuators correction with the feedback of a dynamic interferometer; the interferometer phase ambiguity is solved with an absolute phase sensor measuring a spot across two adjacent segments. Given the peculiarity of the test system, the procedure integrate the reading of both optical sensors with the internal metrology of the M4.

Items.Authors: Luca Oggioni, Riccardo Grignaffini, Runa Antonio Briguglio Pellegrino, Giorgio M. Pariani, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Marco Xompero, Nicolò Azzaroli, Matteo Menessini
Items.Title: Optical calibration of the ELT-M4: Validation of the local calibration of capacitive position sensors on the demonstration prototype
Items.Abstract: We previously introduced a local calibration method for capacitive sensors of deformable mirrors, using sub-aperture interferometry with a push–pull sequence, phase unwrapping and a differential algorithm to derive each actuator’s response. While effective in the lab, applying this procedure to the full-scale Demonstration Prototype (DP) on the ELT-M4 test tower revealed unexpectedly fast and large noise, preventing stable phase unwrapping even at night.  We therefore developed a new strategy: one DP shell is kept fixed and used as an optical reference, while a neighbouring shell is actuated as in the original method. This provides a stable phase anchor for all frames, enabling robust alignment and allowing the differential algorithm to converge. The new approach restores reliable calibration of the capacitive sensors under realistic tower conditions and is fully scalable to the complete M4 system.

Items.Authors: Marcela Izquierdo Poza, Kirit Karkare, John M. Kovac, Colin A. Bischoff, Peter Ade, Zeeshan Ahmed, Mandana Amiri, Denis Barkats, Ritoban Basu Thakur, Dominic Beck, James J. Bock, James Cornerlison, Airel Cukierman, Mike Echter, Miranda Eiben, Brodi D. Elwood, Sofia Fatigoni, Jeffrey P Filippini, Antonio Fortes, Maodong Gao, Christos Giannakopoulos, Neil Goeckner-Wald, David Goldfinger, Annsley Greathouse, Paul Grimes, George Halal, Mark Halpern, Emma Hand, Shawn Henderson, Thuong Hoang, Johannes Hubmayr, Howard Hui, Kent Irwin, Jae H. Kang, Kekoa Lasko, Kenny Lau, Margaret R. Lautzenhiser, Scott Mackey, Nolan Maher, Yuka Nakato, Hien T. Nguyen, Roger O'Brient, Anika Patel, Matthew A. Petroff, Annie R. Polish, Clement Pryke, Carl D. Reintsema, Thibault Romand, Maria Salatino, Benjamin L. Schmitt, Baibhav Singari, Aaron Steiger, Bryan Steinbach, Rashmikant Sudiwala, Keith L Thompson, Clara Vergès, Abigail Vieregg, Albert Wandui, W.L. Kimmy Wu, Cyndia Yu, Lingzhen Zeng, Silvia Zhang
Items.Title: Optical characterization of the BICEP array 150 and 220/270 GHz CMB polarimeters in the 2026 season
Items.Abstract: BICEP Array (BA) measures faint polarization in the cosmic microwave background to test cosmic inflation. Each detector’s angular response needs to be precisely measured since beam mismatch between orthogonally polarized detector pairs can leak temperature into polarization and bias the tensor-to-scalar ratio r.   We present new far-field beam measurements for the 2026 season, focusing on characterizing new detectors at 220/270 GHz in the BA3 receiver and consistency checks at 150 GHz in BA2. We also introduce low-level improvements to the beam mapping analysis pipeline leading to better-quantified noise and higher-fidelity beam shapes. These updates yield more reliable characterization of BA beams and help ensure that our control of beam systematics improves commensurately with our sensitivity and limits on inflation.

Items.Authors: John J. Piotrowski, Danielle Frostig, Daniel Fabricant, Mark Mueller, Ana Bonaca, Phillip A. Cargile, Vedant Chandra, Charles Conroy, Benjamin D. Johnson
Items.Title: Optical design of Boombox: a high-throughput optical spectrograph on dual-hemisphere 6.5-meter telescopes
Items.Abstract: Boombox is a moderate-dispersion optical spectrograph currently being built for the 6.5-meter MMT and Magellan Clay telescope. Boombox, in synergy with the LSST, will provide rapid follow-up spectroscopy of LSST targets to classify the diverse array of expected transient astronomical phenomena and their host galaxies. We present the optical design of Boombox, provide a detailed tolerance analysis, and assess performance dependability on thermal variations. Boombox achieves its scientific goals with a two-channel spectrograph covering 3550 to 10100 Å at R = 1200. The spectrograph uses 36 dedicated optical fibers (1.2" core diameter) from the Via fiber positioning system distributed across a 1-degree field of view. Boombox leverages binary transmission gratings and a high QE deep-depleted CCD261-04 to achieve high throughput. Finally, we discuss the optical design challenges associated with minimizing spectral crosstalk and provide lessons learned for future spectrograph designs.

Items.Authors: John J. Piotrowski, Daniel Fabricant, Charlie Conroy, Ana Bonaca, Vedant Chandra, Phillip A. Cargile, Daniel Catropa, Andrew Cline, Banjamin D. Johnson, Mark Mueller, William Podgorski, Andrew Schalk
Items.Title: Optical design of the Via Instrument: a wide-field radial velocity survey spectrograph on dual-hemisphere 6.5-meter telescopes
Items.Abstract: The Via Project is a 5-year all-sky radial velocity survey and instrument currently being constructed with an expected commission date in 2027. The survey will be conducted simultaneously on the 6.5 m MMT and Magellan Clay telescope. The Via Survey will constrain the dark matter environment of the Milky Way through radial velocity and metallicity measurements of stellar streams and local dwarf galaxies. The survey will also reconstruct the 3D structure and kinematics of cold gas in the local CGM through Na I D absorption tomography. The Via Instrument is composed of the fiber positioning system (FPS) and the bench spectrograph (Viaspec). The FPS distributes ~600 robotically reconfigurable optical fibers across a 1° field of view. Viaspec covers 5050–5950 Å at a resolving power of R = 15,000. The spectrograph utilizes high-efficiency binary gratings and a custom camera lens (f/1.4, EFL = 400mm). We present the optical design, expected performance, and status of instrument.

Items.Authors: Salvador Cuevas, Joel Sánchez-Bermudez, Rebeca Garcia-López, Gerhard Ulbricht, Luis C. Alvarez-Nuñez, Carolina Keiman, Aaron Cruz-Ramirez, Diego Zimarrön-Hernández
Items.Title: Optical verification of the new Ge grism for GRAVITY+ SUPER HIGH-RES mode
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present the optical tests carried out on the high-resolution Ge grism for GRAVITY+. We describe the dimensional tests of the grism ,including the faces angles and the number of lines/mm, using an optical goniometer.   The figure of the faces was measured using a ZYGO VeriFire Fizeau interferometer. We also estimated the roughness of the grism faces by means of an additional optical system coupled to the ZYGO interferometer. Furthermore, we describe an alternative verification of the number of lines/mm using an electronic microscope.   The transmission in the K band at cryogenic temperatures was crucial for the validity of the grism. We describe the optical setup, which includes a special cryostat, and the obtained results in the laboratory of this transmission value.

Items.Authors: florian cheyssial, Cyril Petit, Laurent Mugnier
Items.Title: Optimal exposure time for satellite imaging? A trade-off between residual tip/tilt and registration accuracy
Items.Abstract: Adaptive-Optics corrected astronomical imaging and satellite imaging from the ground share many commonalities but have also specificities. In particular satellites are non-stationary objects in terms of both shape and flux, encouraging shorter exposure time. Besides, very short exposures freeze the turbulence and enable measuring higher spatial frequencies, but at the cost of a low image SNR, which complicates the post processing. Conversely, too long exposures lead to blurred images where high frequency information is lost.    We propose a method for determining the optimal exposure time regarding the image quality after post-processing. Our model is based on the object type and flux, on the residual aberrations power spectral densities and on the noise level. First, we consider the case where the residual aberrations are only tip/tilt residues and telescope's vibrations. Then, we consider the variations of higher order aberrations (i.e. that the PSFs differ from one image to another).

Items.Authors: Yinzi Xin, Sebastiaan Haffert, Rico Landman
Items.Title: Optimal mode-sorting coronagraphy for exoplanet detection and characterization
Items.Abstract: Conventional coronagraph architectures struggle to reach the theoretical limit of exoplanet detection at close working angles. Spatial mode-sorting is capable of reaching the theoretical limit, but the optimal solution has so far only been calculated for a completely unresolved star whose signal lies entirely in the fundamental piston mode of the telescope. This work enables the calculation of optimized nulling modes as a function of the size of the star and planet parameters, with the goal of improving coronagraphic performance at ~lambda/D working angles given partially resolved stars and complex telescope apertures. We perform calculations using quantum information formalism and combine them with numerical optimization techniques to explore the behavior of optimal mode-sorting measurements. We present the optimal modes for measuring planets with known signals and characterize the tradeoffs inherent to coronagraphs for a finite field-of-view.

Items.Authors: Makoto Komaki, Yuji Ikeda, Kenta Sakabe, Shin Oya
Items.Title: Optimal weighting functions and altitude sampling for accurate estimation of Cn² in the MASS method
Items.Abstract: The MASS method observes the scintillation of bright stars through a telescope equipped with multiple apertures to estimate the turbulent contribution at different altitudes (the Cn² profile) from correlations of the scintillation obtained at each aperture.  In this study, we investigated procedures for determining suitable aperture shapes. We identify combinations of aperture geometries (Weighting Functions) whose scintillation curves exhibit distinctive features at particular altitudes. Using the altitude-sensitivity matrix derived from these weighting functions, we conduct simulations to estimate Cn2. To obtain this matrix, we also explore a systematic method for determining optimal altitude sampling - namely, the measurement altitude and number of altitudes - by selecting them so that the altitude-layer vectors are as independent as possible. Finally, we discuss the accuracy of the resulting Cn2 estimates based on our evaluation of this approach.

Items.Authors: Jaganathan Ranganathan, Christopher Hopkins, H. Philip Stahl
Items.Title: Optimization of HWO EAC primary mirror backplane structures using Large Integrated Structure Topology Optimization (LISTO)
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) requires an ultra-stable optical telescope. Critical to this need is an ultra-stiff mass-optimized primary mirror backplane structure. This paper presents how LISTO can optimize HWO backplane structure. LISTO is a novel hybrid optimization framework leveraging machine learning techniques coupled with genetic algorithms in MATLAB to efficiently navigate vast truss configuration design spaces. The system operates within user-defined boundaries and interfaces seamlessly with ANSYS for high-fidelity structural evaluation. LISTO automatically identifies and ranks promising solutions based on mass efficiency while satisfying critical resonance frequency criteria, creating data-driven pathways for design refinements. Key performance metrics demonstrate 1000x computational acceleration compared to conventional design approaches, enabling comprehensive evaluation of backplane structural alternatives within dramatically compressed timeframes.

Items.Authors: Leon Olde Scholtenhuis, Jurre Heeringa, Alkistis Kyriakidou, Nikita A. Soshnin, Kevin Kouwenhoven, David J. Thoen, Jochem Baselmans, Sten Vollebregt, Akira Endo
Items.Title: Optimizing deposition conditions and dielectrics for parallel-plate capacitor KIDs in TIFUUN ifus
Items.Abstract: Probing early-universe star formation with TIFUUN requires an on-chip Integral Field Unit (IFU) containing ~15,000 Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) on a 4-inch wafer. This necessitates compact KID designs, such as Parallel Plate Capacitor (PPC) KIDs.  However, the sensitivity of these devices is often limited by two-level-system (TLS) noise originating in the intra-plate dielectric, whose dependence on deposition conditions remains poorly understood.  Here we present frequency-noise measurements of NbTiN PPC resonators employing ICP-PECVD a-Si:H dielectrics, and relate these results to the corresponding deposition conditions and film properties. Based on these findings, we propose a PPC KID geometry and dielectric process that meets the requirements of TIFUUN’s IFU.
